records.publisher: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
records.shortExcerpt: Rosemary does best in well-drained soils in full sun. Cultural Conditions — Light: Full sun (6+ hours).
records.reviewerSummary: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox. Full sun is the preferred light exposure. Source also notes rosemary tolerates partial shade; treat as tolerance/limitation only, not as a second preferred value. Publication and source-update dates are not displayed. Accepted scientific name Salvia rosmarinus; historic Rosmarinus officinalis is identity note only (no registry write). Rosemary water packets must not be reused as sun evidence.
records.normalizedClaim: Salvia rosmarinus prefers full sun as its primary light exposure in outdoor cultivation.

records.publisher: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources
records.shortExcerpt: Exposure: Full sun. Plant rosemary in full sun.
records.reviewerSummary: UC Cooperative Extension Master Gardeners of San Luis Obispo County; author Polly Nelson, UCCE Master Gardener. Direct full-sun exposure and planting guidance for outdoor rosemary. Indoor/container/overwintering contexts and regional desert heat caveats are limitations only and do not change the outdoor ground mature preference. Humidity/wet-site stress is limitation only. Rosemary water packets must not be reused as sun evidence.
